title: Day 605 — USMCA Round 1 Concludes With 'Net Positive' but No Concrete Agreements; Round 2 Set for June 16-17 Washington
detail: On May 29, 2026 (Day 605), the first formal USMCA bilateral negotiating round concluded at Mexico's Ministry of Economy in Mexico City after two days of sessions (May 28–29). Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard declared a 'saldo positivo' (net positive), citing a 'constructive environment and frank bilateral dialogue' — but explicitly acknowledged that no concrete written agreements had been signed. Mexican trade negotiators described the sessions as a 'productive exchange of positions' rather than breakthrough dealmaking. KEY OUTCOMES: (1) AUTO RULES OF ORIGIN: The U.S. tabled a proposal requiring that at least 50% of each North American vehicle's value originate specifically from the United States — not just North America — a more restrictive formulation than current USMCA rules that requires 75% North American content. Mexico's team responded that such a requirement would disrupt established supply chains in Monterrey, Saltillo, San Luis Potosí, and Guanajuato. No agreement reached. (2) CHINESE NEARSHORING: Both sides agreed to continue working on an 'economic security framework' to address U.S. concerns about Chinese manufacturing investment in Mexico being used to access USMCA zero-tariff treatment — but no enforcement mechanism was defined in Round 1. (3) STEEL AND ALUMINUM: Mexico reiterated its demand for elimination of U.S. Section 232 steel and aluminum tariffs; U.S. side offered 'review mechanisms' without concrete timelines. EBRARD ASSESSMENT: Economy Secretary Ebrard confirmed publicly that the pace of Round 1 makes a clean 16-year USMCA extension by the July 1, 2026 Joint Review deadline 'unlikely' — a provisional agreement extending talks is the more probable outcome. SCHEDULE CONFIRMED: Round 2 is set for June 16–17 in Washington D.C. (agriculture, labor standards, 'level playing field'); Round 3 for the week of July 20 in Mexico City (final consolidation ahead of July 1 deadline). USTR.gov issued a formal statement confirming the conclusion of Round 1 and the Round 2 schedule.

media.caption: USMCA Round 1 concludes May 29 — Ebrard declares 'net positive' but no concrete deals signed; U.S. demands 50% US-origin auto content rejected by Mexico; Round 2 set June 16-17 Washington

title: Day 605 — CNTE Marches to Secretaría de Gobernación; Seven-Hour Talks End Without Agreement; June 1 Strike Escalation Confirmed
detail: On May 29, 2026 (Day 605), approximately 800 CNTE members — led primarily by Sección 22 (Oaxaca), the largest and most militant section — marched to the Secretaría de Gobernación (SEGOB) building at Abraham González 48, Colonia Juárez, Mexico City at approximately 10:30 hours. CNTE representatives entered into a third tripartite dialogue session with SEGOB (represented by Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez) and the SEP (Education Secretary Mario Delgado). OUTCOME: After seven hours of negotiations, no agreements were reached on the union's core demands: (1) Abrogation of the 2007 ISSSTE pension reform (the central demand, which restructured pension systems for post-2007 public sector enrollees, eliminating defined-benefit pensions in favor of AFORE individual accounts); (2) A 100% raise to base salary; (3) Reinstatement of dismissed workers; (4) Return to pre-2019 Education Reform teacher evaluation systems. The government offered partial responses on secondary administrative matters — teacher payroll corrections, housing fund regularization — but refused to commit to pension or salary demands, citing fiscal constraints and the 2025 budget framework. ESCALATION ANNOUNCED: The CNTE's national coordinating body formally confirmed that June 1, 2026 mobilizations would proceed as planned — including a mega-march from the Ángel de la Independencia toward the Zócalo in Mexico City (where the FIFA World Cup Fan Fest is being installed), as well as potential blockades at the NAICM/AICM airports and key highway intersections nationwide. Sección 7 (Chiapas), Sección 18 (Michoacán), and sections in Guerrero and Hidalgo announced solidarity actions. CONTEXT: The CNTE strike began May 25, with the June 1 FIFA World Cup opening weekend providing maximum international visibility leverage. Sheinbaum characterized the negotiations at subsequent mañaneras as 'ongoing' and described the CNTE as representing 'some teachers, not all.'

media.caption: CNTE marches to SEGOB May 29 — 800 teachers block entrance, 7-hour talks fail on pension and salary demands, June 1 escalation confirmed ahead of FIFA World Cup opening weekend

title: Day 605 — Mañanera: Sheinbaum Gives Away World Cup Opening-Match Ticket to Indigenous Woman from Veracruz; Culture Ministry Premieres 'La Niña Futbolista'
detail: At her May 29, 2026 (Day 605) morning mañanera, President Sheinbaum made good on her earlier promise to give away her personal presidential inauguration-match ticket for the FIFA World Cup 2026. The ticket — for the tournament's opening match on June 11 at Estadio Azteca (Mexico vs. South Africa) — was awarded to Yolett Cervantes Cuaquehua, a 21-year-old Indigenous woman from Veracruz. Three additional presidential match tickets (for games in Mexico City, Guadalajara, and Monterrey) were given to amateur athletes aged 16, 22, and 23. Sheinbaum stated she would personally watch the opening match at the Zócalo's official FIFA Fan Fest public screening. The Culture Secretariat, under Secretary Claudia Curiel de Icaza, premiered a new recording of 'La niña futbolista' by Julieta Venegas — a song aimed at inspiring girls to pursue soccer — as part of the government's World Cup social campaign. The press conference highlighted Mexico's preparations for hosting the June 11–July 19 tournament and reinforced the administration's messaging around inclusive, popular access to the sporting event.

media.caption: Sheinbaum gives away her World Cup opening-match ticket to Yolett Cervantes Cuaquehua, a 21-year-old indigenous woman from Veracruz; says she will watch at Zócalo Fan Fest
